'''Cazuela''' ({{IPA|es|kaˈθwela|pron}} or {{IPA|es|kaˈswela|}}) is the common name given to a variety of [[Dish (food)|dishes]], especially from [[South America]]. It receives its name from the cazuela (Spanish for '[[cooking pot]]')—traditionally, an often shallow pot made of [[Ceramic glaze|unglazed]] [[earthenware]] used for cooking.<ref>{{Cite web |title=cazuela |url=https://dle.rae.es/cazuela |access-date=2023-08-08 |website=dle.rae.es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Caro Bellido |first=Antonio |title=Diccionario de términos cerámicos y de alfarería |publisher=Agrija Ediciones |year=2008 |isbn=978-84-96191-07-5 |location=Cádiz |pages=69}}</ref> The ingredients and preparation vary from region to region, but it is usually a mid-thick flavoured [[stock (food)|stock]] obtained from [[cooking]] several kinds of [[meat]]s and [[vegetable]]s mixed together.
